batchId: Claude manual-research batch dc-01 (4 DC identities from the Needs manual research list)
method: Web search snippets from the cited pages; claims the snippet did not support were left out or listed under unknowns. No numeric tiers or win probabilities. All records stay provisional until a different contributor checks the cited support.
baselineContinuity: Mainline DC Comics unless a record says otherwise.

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics Doomsday, first seen in Superman: The Man of Steel #17-18 (1992). Excludes Injustice, DCEU, DC Animated Universe and Smallville versions.
characters.summary: Genetically engineered Kryptonian monster who killed Superman. Sources credit him with super strength, invulnerability, speed and a healing factor, and describe a version that copies the powers of beings near him.

techniques: copies powers of nearby super-beings (absorption cells, as described by one secondary source)

mobility: super speed and superhuman agility (publisher power list)

conditional.dependsOn: Specific era or version; not established for every Doomsday story

feats.citation: Superman wiki entry for Doomsday (Death of Superman storyline)

weaknesses: No sourced weakness in the cited pages; reviewer should add one from specific issues
Described as feral and mindless in the early Superman stories, which limits planning
unknowns: No sourced top strength or speed tier.
Which later versions (Rebirth, New 52) keep absorption not checked.

sources.supports: Publisher profile: first appearance Man of Steel (1992); powers listed as super strength, invulnerability, super speed, healing factor, superhuman agility, toxikinesis
Debut Man of Steel #17 (Nov 1992), created by Dan Jurgens; genetically engineered Kryptonian; beat Superman to death; abilities strength, speed, regeneration
Describes absorption cells that copy powers of nearby super-beings, and Doomsday returning stronger after death (secondary source, cites DC wiki pages)
Notes that later Doomsday versions mimicked powers of Superman's team and that the Doomslayer variant appeared

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics John Stewart as an Oan power-ring Green Lantern (debut Green Lantern vol. 2 #87, 1971). Excludes Justice League animation, Injustice and the Sixth Dimension White Lantern version.
characters.summary: Marine veteran and architect, the third human Green Lantern, whose ring makes hard-light constructs, flight and a protective field. His main edge is construct craft and tactical skill, not innate powers.
weaknesses: Classic ring weakness to yellow (one source says his ring still has it)
Powers come from the ring, not from John himself
unknowns: No sourced issue-level feat in this pass.
Whether the yellow weakness holds in Prime Earth was not confirmed.

sources.supports: Publisher profile: third human to wield a Green Lantern ring, USMC veteran, chooses not to wear a mask
First appearance Green Lantern #87 (1971); powers: energy constructs, force field, energy projection, flight; personal skills: will, sniper skills, leadership
Ring gives flight and limited invulnerability; John's ring still has the yellow weakness; ring limited only by imagination (fan blog, secondary)
Wikipedia mirror: debut Green Lantern vol. 2 #87 (Dec 1971), architect and US Marine veteran, abilities: wields Oan power ring

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics Mera of Xebel and Dimension Aqua, Aquaman's wife (New Earth and Prime Earth). Excludes Flashpoint, Justice, Smallville and film versions.
characters.summary: Atlantean-allied queen from Dimension Aqua who controls water, hardening it into weapons and constructs. Sources give her superhuman strength and note a lead vulnerability.

techniques: hard water objects such as water missiles
offense.range: short to long range wherever water is available

mobility: Can travel between Dimension Aqua and Earth
Can propel herself through the air with enough nearby water (Looper)

conditional.dependsOn: Nearby water; exposure to lead removes the power

weaknesses: Exposure to lead removes her hard-water powers
Power depends on water being available
unknowns: Strength figure (70 tons carried) is one wiki's estimate, not a cited issue.

sources.supports: New Earth profile: creates hard water objects, commonly water missiles
Gills, hydrokinesis (hard water), dimensional travel, vulnerability to lead
Can control massive amounts of water to pull an army out to sea; lead removes her hydrokinesis
Considerable superhuman strength, carrying capacity of at least 70 tons (Comic Vine estimate)
Can extract water from other sources and propel herself through the air if enough water is nearby

characters.continuity: Mainline DC Comics Christopher Smith Peacemaker (post-Crisis, 1988 miniseries onward). Excludes the Charlton-era original and John Cena's DCEU/DCU version.
characters.summary: Non-powered soldier-vigilante who relies on marksmanship, hand-to-hand skill and a specialised helmet. He is dangerous through gear and training, with no superhuman defenses.
mobility: Flight pack and custom aircraft in some eras

conditional.ability: Helmet laser, ultrasonic beam and voice duplication
conditional.dependsOn: Charlton-era equipment list; not confirmed for the post-Crisis version

weaknesses: Documented mental illness, hallucinations of his dead father, in the New Earth version
unknowns: Helmet functions cited come from a Charlton-era profile and may differ post-Crisis.
No issue-level feat was captured in this pass.

sources.supports: Publisher profile: powers listed as combat skill, top-level marksman, weapons expert
Abilities: master marksman, skilled hand-to-hand combatant, utilizes helmets that grant abilities
Peacemaker has no powers; strength lies in brains and designed gear
Wikipedia mirror infobox: peak human condition, body armor, flight pack, communications helmet, advanced military weapons
New Earth profile: mental disorder with hallucinations and belief that dead victims speak through his helmet
Charlton-era helmet equipment: laser, ultrasonic beam, voice duplication, plus custom jet (Charlton version, not post-Crisis)
